p: Salcey makes a great starting point for exploring a part of England that often gets overlooked. Just to the west, Stoke Bruerne is a picturesque canal village on the Grand Union Canal, with a flight of locks, pubs by the water and the Canal Museum telling the story of life on the cut. It's a lovely, relaxed follow-up to a morning of zip wires.

Northampton itself is famous for shoemaking, and that heritage still shows around the town. Delapré Abbey, a historic house with gardens and parkland, is a peaceful place for a walk and a cuppa. Design fans should look up 78 Derngate, a townhouse remodelled by Charles Rennie Mackintosh, which is a real gem.
Motorsport lovers won't need reminding that Silverstone isn't far from Salcey, so a weekend could easily combine treetops with something a bit faster.

Back at the forest, a couple of hours is the time to plan for your session, plus a few minutes to get your bearings. Arrive early if you're bringing a dog for the walks, as some trails are busier than others at peak times. If any of the group are nervous of heights, the treetop walkway is a gentle way to test the waters before they commit to booking the full course on another visit.
Wear sturdy shoes and expect mud after rain; this is ancient woodland, and its clay paths do get squelchy.
